mainTopic: Acquiring food for an עירוב with money, the four special times of the year, and the rule that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה in עירובין
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about giving money to a grocer or baker to buy food for an עירוב. The חכמים agree that money given to any other person works, and רבי יהודה adds that an עירוב חצירות may be made even without a person's knowledge, because זכין לאדם שלא בפניו. The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר can let money acquire without משיכה. It answers that he modeled this on the four special times of the year, when a butcher can be forced to slaughter for a customer who only paid. Two explanations of that butcher משנה follow. רבי שמואל בר יצחק says a third person acquired the meat for the buyer, which works only when it benefits him. רב אילא, in the name of רבי יוחנן, says that on those days the חכמים let the Torah rule stand, that money acquires. The גמרא then explains that 'all other people' means a בעל הבית. שמואל also limits the חכמים' ruling to a baker, to a coin, and to the words 'זכה לי'. Finally, שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה in עירובין, but not in laws of מחיצות. רב אחא asks why a ruling is needed if רבי יהודה only explains the חכמים, and the גמרא begins a new answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The חכמים agree that with anyone else the money works
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים, who argued with רבי אליעזר about a grocer or baker, agree that when money is given to any other person for an עירוב, it works, because an עירוב needs the person's consent and he showed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים agree that with all other people, the money does acquire for him, because an עירוב is made for a person only with his knowledge and agreement.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us where the חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר: if you give money to a regular person, not a grocer or baker, the עירוב works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a grocer or baker, the חכמים say the buyer is just making a purchase, not appointing a שליח, and money alone does not complete a purchase. With anyone else, giving money for an עירוב clearly means 'please be my agent', and that is exactly the consent an עירוב needs. So the dispute is only about shopkeepers, not about everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: They agree (the opposing side concedes a point)
His money acquired for him (the payment worked)
We make an עירוב
With his knowledge and consent

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the חכמים reject the use of money completely. They only reject it with a grocer or baker. With anyone else they agree that it works.

phrases.english: And they (the Sages) agree regarding all other people,
phrases.notes: Other than a grocer or baker, who were discussed earlier in the משנה.

phrases.english: that his money acquires for him.
phrases.notes: Giving the money makes that person his agent to set up the עירוב.

phrases.english: for one does not make an eruv for a person
phrases.notes: This is the reason.

phrases.english: except with his knowledge.
phrases.notes: Handing over the money shows his consent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדִים בִּשְׁאָר כׇּל הָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's dispute between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With anyone other than a grocer or baker, money given for an עירוב is effective, because the giver has shown consent and appointed an agent.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the consent rule to עירובי תחומין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the need for consent applies only to עירובי תחומין. An עירוב חצירות can be made even without the person's knowledge, because it is purely a benefit to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When does this rule apply? With עירובי תחומין. But with עירובי חצירות, we may make an עירוב for someone whether he knows or not, because you may do something good for a person when he is not there, but you may not do something bad for him when he is not there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה narrows the rule we just heard, that an עירוב needs the person's consent. He says it only applies to a boundary עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב חצירות only helps, because it lets everyone carry in the shared courtyard, so we can do it for him without asking. An עירוב תחומין lets him walk farther in one direction but takes away his walking room in the other direction. Since it has a downside, we need his consent. The principle is זכין לאדם שלא בפניו, ואין חבין לאדם שלא בפניו.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (a formula for limiting a rule)
עירובין that extend the שבת walking boundary
עירובין that join courtyards so that carrying is allowed
One may act for a person's benefit when he is not present
One may not act to a person's disadvantage when he is not present

steps.whatToRemember: An עירוב חצירות is pure benefit, so it does not need the person's consent. An עירוב תחומין has a cost as well as a benefit, so it does need consent.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of זכין לאדם שלא בפניו is a basic principle of agency that comes up all over ש"ס, for example in giving gifts and acquiring things on behalf of others.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: He is setting up a limitation on the rule that consent is needed.

phrases.english: With regard to boundary eruvs,
but with regard to courtyard eruvs,
one may make an eruv with his knowledge or without his knowledge,
because one may act for a person's benefit in his absence,
phrases.notes: A courtyard עירוב only helps him.

phrases.english: but one may not act to a person's disadvantage in his absence.
phrases.notes: A boundary עירוב takes away his walking room in the opposite direction.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule from step 1 that an עירוב requires the person's consent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The consent requirement applies only to עירובי תחומין. עירובי חצירות may be made without the person's knowledge, because it is a benefit to him.

steps.title: How can money work when the buyer never pulled the food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי אליעזר's reason. Normally a buyer acquires movable items only through משיכה, so how can money given to a grocer acquire the food?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is רבי אליעזר's reason? But the buyer never pulled the food into his possession!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking how רבי אליעזר can say the grocer case works, since the normal way to acquire a movable item is by pulling it, and that never happened here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a grocer, the buyer is purchasing food, not appointing an agent. For movable items, money by itself does not complete a sale. The act of acquiring is משיכה, pulling the item. Since the buyer never pulled anything, the food should not be his, and the עירוב should fail.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that analyzes the משנה
What is the reason?
Pulled. משיכה is the act of acquiring movable items.

phrases.english: Gemara: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?
phrases.notes: Why does he hold that money given to a grocer acquires the food?

phrases.english: But he did not pull!
phrases.notes: Money without משיכה does not normally acquire movable items.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר? הָא לֹא מָשַׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by questioning רבי אליעזר's view from the earlier part of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the basis for רבי אליעזר's ruling that money given to a grocer or baker acquires the food, when no משיכה was done?
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that זכו לו מעותיו in the case of a grocer or baker
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Movable items are acquired by משיכה, not by money alone. Without pulling, the buyer should not own the food.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר treated it like the four special times of the year
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבהו, explains that רבי אליעזר treated this case like the four times a year when paying money alone is enough, even without pulling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבהו: רבי אליעזר made it like the four special times of the year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: רבי אליעזר compared this case to four special times in the year when money alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four times of the year when paying money is enough without משיכה, as the next step will show. רבי אליעזר applies that same rule to buying food for an עירוב. The question was 'he didn't pull!', and the answer is that in this kind of special situation, pulling is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it (treated it as)
The four special times of the year (the days before פסח, שבועות, ראש השנה, and שמיני עצרת)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבָהוּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avahu said:
Rabbi Eliezer made it
phrases.notes: He treated the עירוב purchase as...

phrases.english: like the four times in the year,
phrases.notes: These are times when paying money alone is effective.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבָהוּ: עֲשָׂאוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר treated buying food for an עירוב like the four special times of the year, when money is effective even without משיכה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Analogy to an established special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since there was no משיכה, the purchase should fail.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like the four special times, this situation lets money work without pulling.

steps.title: The משנה about forcing the butcher to slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה as the source: on the four special times, a butcher can be forced to slaughter even a very expensive ox for a customer who paid only one dinar.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: On these four times of the year, we make the butcher slaughter against his will. Even if the ox is worth a thousand dinar and the buyer has paid only one dinar, we force him to slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the four special times: a משנה saying that on those days money alone obligates the butcher to slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if the buyer never pulled the meat, the butcher could back out of the sale. On these four busy times, the money alone binds the butcher, even if it costs him a huge loss to slaughter a whole ox for one customer's small portion. This shows that money works without משיכה at those times, which is the model רבי אליעזר used for the עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: We make (someone) slaughter
Butcher
Against his will
We force

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's view is based on the four special times of the year, when money obligates the seller even without משיכה. He applies the same idea to buying food for an עירוב.

phrases.english: As we learned: On these four times,
phrases.notes: The days before פסח, שבועות, ראש השנה, and שמיני עצרת.

phrases.english: we make the butcher slaughter against his will.
Even if the ox is worth a thousand dinar
and the buyer has paid only one dinar,
phrases.notes: The butcher may end up stuck with the rest of the meat.

phrases.english: we force him to slaughter.
phrases.notes: The money alone binds the butcher, without משיכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: בְּאַרְבָּעָה פְּרָקִים אֵלּוּ מַשְׁחִיטִין אֶת הַטַּבָּח בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the 'four times of the year' mentioned in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That at the four special times of the year, money is effective without משיכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה stating that on the four times a butcher is forced to slaughter, even an ox worth a thousand dinar for a buyer of one dinar

steps.title: The משנה continues: if the ox dies, the buyer loses
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the quoted משנה rules that on the four special times, if the ox dies, the loss falls on the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, if the ox died, it died at the buyer's loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the butcher משנה from Step 5. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the buyer's dinar counts on these special days, part of the ox is treated as his. So if the ox dies, he loses his dinar and cannot get it back.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore. It draws a result from what was just said.
The buyer

phrases.english: Therefore, if it died,
it died for the buyer (the buyer takes the loss).

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ אִם מֵת, מֵת לַלּוֹקֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה quoted in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: Who bears the loss when the ox dies on the four special times
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the butcher on the four special times

steps.title: Why should the buyer lose if he never pulled the ox?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the buyer did not do משיכה, so why is the ox his loss?
steps.simpleTranslation: It died at the buyer's loss? But he did not pull it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by the משנה's ruling and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Movable items are normally acquired only by משיכה. If the buyer never pulled the ox, it seems he never truly owned any of it. So he should get his dinar back when it dies.

keyTerms.meaning: But he did not pull it! (He did not do the act of acquiring.)

phrases.english: It died for the buyer?
But he did not pull it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת לַלּוֹקֵחַ? הָא לֹא מָשַׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling just quoted in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the buyer takes the loss
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without משיכה, full ownership of movable items does not pass. So the loss should belong to the seller.

steps.title: רב הונא: the buyer did pull the ox
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the משנה is talking about a case where the buyer actually did משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is talking about a case where he did pull it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the challenge by reading the משנה as a case where the buyer pulled the ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the buyer did משיכה, he clearly owned his share. Then it makes sense that the loss is his. This answer is about to be tested against the next line of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he pulled it

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is a case where he pulled it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בְּשֶׁמָּשַׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The buyer never pulled the ox, so the loss should not be his.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about a buyer who did pull, so the loss is his.

steps.title: The משנה's second half disproves רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: If the buyer pulled the ox, why does the משנה say that on ordinary days the loss falls on the seller?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the משנה: On the rest of the days of the year it is not so. Therefore, if it died, it died at the seller's loss. Why? He pulled it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא using the second half of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the same case for ordinary days and says the seller takes the loss. If the buyer had pulled the ox, he would own it on any day. So רב הונא's reading cannot work for the second half.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Look at the end (last part) of the משנה
The seller
Why?

steps.confusionAlert: Both halves of the משנה describe the same case. The only difference is the time of year. So whatever answer you give must work for both halves.

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
On the rest of the days of the year it is not so.
Therefore, if it died, it died for the seller.
Why? He pulled it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of רב הונא in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the buyer pulled the ox
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pulling the ox works all year round. So the seller could never take the loss on ordinary days, yet the משנה says he does.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר יצחק: someone else acquired it for the buyer
steps.stepSummary: The buyer did not pull the ox himself. The butcher had another person acquire the meat for him, without his knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר יצחק said: Really, the buyer did not pull it. Here we are dealing with a case where the butcher gave it to him through another person.
steps.whatsHappening: A new answer replaces רב הונא's. It explains both halves of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer did not pull the ox himself. The butcher had a third person acquire a dinar's worth of meat for him without asking him. Whether that works depends on whether it helps or hurts the buyer, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. It brings us back to the original assumption.
What case are we dealing with here?
He gave him ownership through another person

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said:
Actually, it is where he did not pull it;
with what are we dealing here?
Where he conferred possession on him through another person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק: לְעוֹלָם בְּשֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops רב הונא's answer after the challenge in Step 9 and gives a new reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either the buyer pulled the ox or he had no act of acquiring at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: A third person acquired the meat for the buyer without his knowledge.

steps.title: A benefit can be given without the buyer present, a burden cannot
steps.stepSummary: On the four special times, getting meat is a benefit, so it can be acquired for the buyer without his knowledge. On other days it is a burden, so it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: At these four times, when it is a benefit to him, we may acquire for him when he is not there. On the rest of the days of the year, when it is a burden to him, we may not do something against him unless he is there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי שמואל בר יצחק's answer. It explains why the same act works on the special days and fails on ordinary days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the special days everyone wants meat, so the purchase helps the buyer. The rule זכין לאדם שלא בפניו lets the third person acquire it for him, and the loss is the buyer's. On ordinary days he may not want meat and would owe money, so the purchase hurts him. The rule אין חבין לאדם אלא בפניו means it fails, and the loss is the seller's.

keyTerms.meaning: A benefit
We may acquire for a person when he is not there
A burden, something against him
We may not act against a person unless he is there
Times or seasons of the year

steps.whatToRemember: The same act can succeed or fail depending on whether it helps or hurts the person. A benefit can be done for someone without his knowledge (זכין לאדם שלא בפניו). A burden cannot (אין חבין לאדם אלא בפניו).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same idea רבי יהודה used in Step 2. An עירוב חצירות can be made without a person's knowledge because it is purely a benefit to him.

phrases.english: At these four times
when it is a benefit for him,
one may acquire for him in his absence.
On the rest of the days of the year,
when it is a disadvantage for him,
one may act to his disadvantage only in his presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאַרְבָּעָה פְּרָקִים אֵלּוּ דִּזְכוּת הוּא לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of Step 10 by explaining both halves of the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The butcher משנה fits both halves. Acquiring for someone else works when it benefits him (the four special times) and fails when it is a burden (the rest of the year).

steps.title: רב אילא: At the four times the חכמים followed Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב אילא, quoting רבי יוחנן, explains the four special times differently: at those times the חכמים let the Torah's rule apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אילא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: At these four times of the year, the חכמים based their ruling on Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another answer to the question of why the ox is the buyer's loss even though he never pulled it. This answer is an alternative to both רב הונא (the buyer pulled) and רבי שמואל בר יצחק (a third party acquired for him).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers needed some act of acquisition: רב הונא said the buyer pulled, and רבי שמואל בר יצחק said a third party acquired for him. רב אילא does not need any of that. At these four times the חכמים set aside their own rule and let Torah law stand, so the buyer's money alone made his share of the ox his.

keyTerms.meaning: The four special times of the year when people buy a lot of meat
The חכמים set their ruling in place
Torah law, the original law before any rabbinic decree

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a continuation of רבי שמואל בר יצחק's answer. It is a separate explanation that does not need anyone to do משיכה or acquire on the buyer's behalf at all.

phrases.english: And Rav Ila said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
At these four times of the year
the Sages established their ruling
based on Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אִילָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different resolution to the challenge raised in step 7. It is an alternative to רב הונא's answer (step 8) and to רבי שמואל בר יצחק's answer (steps 10–11).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Change of legal basis: Torah law applies on these days, so no משיכה is needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the buyer could only own the ox through משיכה, so someone had to pull it for him.
steps.terutzMaskana: On the four special times, money acquires just as it does under Torah law, so the buyer owns the ox once he pays.

steps.title: By Torah law money acquires; pulling is a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the background: by Torah law money buys movable items, and the חכמים required משיכה only as a protective decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: By Torah law, money acquires. So why did the חכמים say that pulling is what acquires? It is a decree, out of concern that the seller will say to the buyer: 'Your wheat got burned in the attic.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the source behind רב אילא's statement: what Torah law is, and why the חכמים normally changed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under Torah law, paying for an item makes it the buyer's, wherever it is. The חכמים worried that once a seller has been paid, he will not bother to protect goods that are no longer his. If a fire breaks out, he can simply say 'your wheat burned.' So they ruled that a sale is final only once the buyer pulls the item. At the four special times, they let the original Torah law stand.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
Money acquires, meaning payment alone completes the purchase
Pulling, the physical act of acquiring a movable item
A protective decree made by the חכמים
Attic or upper floor

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic framework for how movable items are bought in הלכה: money works by Torah law, but rabbinic law requires משיכה. It also explains how רבי אליעזר in our משנה can say that money acquires food for an עירוב.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
By Torah law, money acquires.
And why did they say that pulling acquires?
It is a decree, lest the seller say to him:
Your wheat was burned in the attic.
phrases.notes: Once paid, the seller has no reason to protect goods that already belong to the buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה, מָעוֹת קוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the legal background that makes sense of step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law money acquires movable items. משיכה is required only by rabbinic decree, out of concern that a paid seller will be careless with the goods.
steps.whatToRemember: Two surviving explanations of the four special times: רבי שמואל בר יצחק says a third party acquired the meat for the buyer, which works because it is a benefit to him; רב אילא says that at those times money acquires, as it does under Torah law. (רב הונא's answer that the buyer pulled was rejected.)

steps.title: Who are 'all other people' in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to our משנה and asks who is meant by 'all other people,' where even the חכמים agree that money acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they agree regarding all other people...' Who are these 'all other people'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words of our משנה about the עירוב and asks for a definition. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said that giving a coin to a baker does not acquire the עירוב food. However, they agree that it works with 'all other people.' The גמרא wants to know exactly who falls into that group.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree, meaning the חכמים concede
All other people
Who?

phrases.english: The Mishnah stated: And they agree regarding all other people, etc.
Who are 'all other people'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדִים בִּשְׁאָר כׇּל הָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the four special times and returns to the next phrase of our משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is meant by 'all other people' in the משנה.

steps.title: רב: It means a homeowner
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that 'all other people' means a בעל הבית, an ordinary person who is not a merchant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It means a בעל הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question: 'all other people' means an ordinary homeowner, not a shopkeeper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baker who takes the coin is selling his own bread, so the rabbinic rule that a sale needs משיכה applies. A בעל הבית who takes the coin is not selling. He is acting as the person's agent to acquire the food on his behalf, so the coin does work.

keyTerms.meaning: A homeowner, an ordinary person who is not a merchant

phrases.english: Rav said:
A homeowner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'All other people' refers to a בעל הבית, not a merchant.

steps.title: שמואל agrees: only a baker is excluded
steps.stepSummary: שמואל also says it means a בעל הבית. This is shown from his statement that the חכמים' rule applies only to a baker.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל likewise said: a בעל הבית. As שמואל said: They taught this only about a baker, but a בעל הבית does acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל holds the same view as רב, and quotes a statement of his that proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל limits the חכמים' ruling ('his money does not acquire') to a baker. With a בעל הבית, the money does acquire. This is the same as רב's definition of 'all other people.'

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise, meaning another sage agrees
They taught this only in the case of, a phrase that limits a ruling
Baker

phrases.english: And likewise Shmuel said: A homeowner.
As Shmuel said:
They taught this only about a baker,
but a homeowner does acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds שמואל as agreeing with רב's answer in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That 'all other people' means a בעל הבית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's statement: 'They taught this only about a baker, but a בעל הבית acquires.'

steps.title: שמואל: The rule is only about a coin, not a utensil
steps.stepSummary: שמואל adds a second limit: the חכמים' ruling applies only when a coin was given. If a utensil was given, it acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: They taught this only when he gave a מעה, but if he gave a utensil, it acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives another limit on the חכמים' ruling: it applies only when a coin was handed over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A coin cannot be used for חליפין, the exchange method of acquiring. A utensil can. If the person gives the baker a utensil in exchange for the food, he acquires the food through חליפין, wherever the food is, even without משיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A small coin
A utensil or object
Acquiring by exchange, which works with an object but not with coins

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים' rule that money does not acquire the עירוב has two limits, both from שמואל: it applies only to a baker (not a בעל הבית), and only to a coin (not a utensil).
steps.confusionAlert: The utensil does not work as payment. It works through a different method of acquiring, חליפין (exchange).

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
They taught this only about a coin,
but a utensil does acquire.
phrases.notes: Through חליפין, exchange.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit, from שמואל, on the חכמים' ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים' ruling applies only when a coin is given. Giving a utensil acquires the food through חליפין.

steps.title: שמואל's third limit: 'acquire for me' versus 'make an עירוב for me'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the חכמים' ruling applies only when the person told the baker 'זכה לי.' If he said 'ערב לי,' he made the baker his שליח, and the עירוב works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: They only taught this when he said to him 'Acquire for me.' But if he said 'Make an עירוב for me,' he made him his agent, and it acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds a third limit to the חכמים' ruling that giving a coin to a baker does not get you the עירוב. It depends on the exact words the person used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'זכה לי' sounds like buying the food, and buying movable items needs משיכה, not just money. Saying 'ערב לי' asks the baker to set up the עירוב himself as a שליח. That is an appointment, not a sale, so the coin-versus-משיכה problem never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Acquire for me': sounds like a purchase
'Make an עירוב for me': a request to set it up
He made him his agent
'They only taught this when': a phrase that limits a ruling

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים' ruling now has three limits: it applies only to a baker, only when a coin was given, and only when the person said 'זכה לי.'

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא דְּאָמַר לוֹ ״זְכֵה לִי״,
phrases.english: They only taught this when he said to him, 'Acquire for me,'
phrases.notes: This is the language of buying, so the money-without-משיכה problem applies.

phrases.english: but if he said, 'Make an eruv for me,'
he made him an agent, and it acquires.
phrases.notes: The baker sets up the עירוב on his behalf.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא דְּאָמַר לוֹ ״זְכֵה לִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the third in a series of limits שמואל places on the חכמים' ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים' ruling applies only to the wording 'זכה לי.' With 'ערב לי' the baker is a שליח and the עירוב works.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה in all matters of עירובין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites רבי יהודה's statement in the משנה. רב יהודה, in the name of שמואל, rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה here and wherever he taught about עירובין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'רבי יהודה said: When is this said? ...' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה. And not only that, but wherever רבי יהודה taught a law in עירובין, the הלכה follows him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, where רבי יהודה limits 'you may only make an עירוב with a person's knowledge' to עירובי תחומין. שמואל rules like רבי יהודה and then makes the ruling general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says עירובי חצירות may be made even without the person's knowledge, because it is a benefit to him. שמואל agrees, and adds a broad rule: in עירובין, the הלכה always follows רבי יהודה. That broad rule sets up the next question about how far it reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When is this said?': a phrase that limits a rule
The final ruling follows him
'And not only that, but': widens a ruling
An עירוב joining courtyards so people may carry between them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי יהודה (the תנא in the משנה) with רב יהודה (the אמורא, a student of שמואל). Here רב יהודה is reporting a ruling that follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a major rule for deciding הלכה across all of מסכת עירובין.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה.

phrases.english: In what case is this said, etc.
phrases.notes: In the משנה: it applies to עירובי תחומין, but not to עירובי חצירות.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
and not only that, but

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּעֵירוּבִין
phrases.english: any place where Rabbi Yehuda taught concerning eruvin,
the halacha follows him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts a new section on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה here, and in every ruling he taught about עירובין.

steps.title: Does the rule include an alleyway whose beam or side post was removed?
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בגדתאה asks רב יהודה whether שמואל's broad rule also covers רבי יהודה's view about an alleyway whose beam or side post was removed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בגדתאה said to רב יהודה: Did שמואל say this even about an alleyway whose beams or side posts were removed?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone tests how far the broad rule goes. He asks whether it also covers a famous ruling of רבי יהודה about an alleyway that lost its beam or side post during שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere, רבי יהודה rules that if carrying in an alleyway was permitted when שבת began, it stays permitted for that שבת even after the קורה or לחי is removed. רב חנא asks whether 'everywhere in עירובין' also includes this ruling about the walls and markers of an alleyway.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway onto which courtyards open
A crossbeam over the entrance of an alleyway
A side post at the entrance of an alleyway
From Baghdad

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה לְרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Chana from Baghdad said to Rav Yehuda:
Did Shmuel say this even about an alleyway
whose crossbeams or side posts were removed?
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה permits carrying there for the rest of that שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This asks about the scope of the broad rule given in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'every place in עירובין' include רבי יהודה's ruling about an alleyway that lost its beam or side post?

steps.title: The rule covers עירובין, not מחיצות
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that שמואל's rule covers the laws of עירובין only, not the laws of מחיצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I told you about עירובין, not about partitions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question and sets the limit of the broad rule. It does not include laws about walls and partitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beams and side posts belong to the laws of מחיצות, which are a separate area from the laws of making an עירוב. So in the alleyway case, the הלכה does not automatically follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Partitions, walls, and markers that define an area
I told you

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה in עירובין' covers the laws of making an עירוב, but not the laws of מחיצות such as a קורה or לחי.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I told you about eruvin,
and not about partitions.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעֵירוּבִין אָמַרְתִּי לְךָ, וְלֹא בִּמְחִיצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. שמואל's rule covers עירובין only. Laws of partitions, such as a removed beam or side post, are not included.

steps.title: Why say 'the הלכה follows' if there is no dispute?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges רב אשי. Ruling 'הלכה כרבי יהודה' implies that someone disagrees with him. But רבי יהושע בן לוי said that רבי יהודה's 'אימתי' and 'במה' statements only explain the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: You say 'the הלכה follows him,' which implies there is a dispute. But didn't רבי יהושע בן לוי say: every place in our משנה where רבי יהודה says 'when?' or 'in what case?', he is only explaining the words of the חכמים!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא attacks שמואל's ruling from Step 19. You only say 'the הלכה follows X' when there is an argument. Here, though, there may be no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יהודה opens with 'במה דברים אמורים' ('in what case was this said?'). According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, that wording means he is clarifying the חכמים, not arguing with them. If so, why would שמואל need to say 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה'?

keyTerms.meaning: This implies that they argue
'When?': a word רבי יהודה uses to set a limit
'In what case?': another limiting word
To explain the words of the חכמים, not to argue with them

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב אחא is arguing about the actual law of עירוב here. His question is only about the wording 'הלכה', which normally assumes there is a disagreement.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole section that follows. Do רבי יהודה and the חכמים really argue about informing people of an עירוב, or not?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
'The halacha is' implies that they argue.
phrases.notes: Referring to שמואל's ruling in Step 19.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
Every place where Rabbi Yehuda said
'when' or 'in what case' in our Mishnah,
he comes only to explain the words of the Sages!

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הֲלָכָה״, מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיגִי. וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in Step 19 that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement 'הלכה כרבי יהודה' in our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'הלכה' assumes a dispute. Yet רבי יהושע בן לוי says רבי יהודה's 'במה' statements only explain the חכמים, so there is no dispute to decide.

steps.title: Do they really not argue? A משנה requires informing
steps.stepSummary: Before answering, the גמרא questions the idea that there is no dispute at all. An earlier משנה rules that new residents must be informed of an עירוב, which seems to go against רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do they really not argue? But we learned in a משנה: if new residents were added to the alleyway, he adds to the עירוב, gives them a share, and must inform them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יהושע בן לוי's claim. It brings a משנה that seems to show someone does disagree with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that for an עירוב of courtyards you can give someone a share without his knowledge, since it is a benefit to him. The earlier משנה says you must inform the new residents. That sounds like a תנא who disagrees with רבי יהודה, so there would be a real dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה
New residents were added to them
He adds to the food and gives them a share in it
He must inform them

steps.confusionAlert: This question is aimed at רבי יהושע בן לוי's 'no dispute' idea, not at רב אחא. The גמרא pauses the main question to ask whether its starting point is even true.

phrases.english: And do they not argue?
But we learned in a Mishnah:
If new residents were added to them,
he adds and grants them a share, and he must inform them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי? וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the 'no dispute' premise that the challenge in Step 22 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה and the חכמים do not argue
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה requires informing new residents. That contradicts רבי יהודה's view that a benefit can be given without the person's knowledge, so some תנא must disagree with him.

steps.title: That משנה is about a courtyard between two alleyways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה requiring notice deals with a courtyard between two alleyways. In that case joining one alleyway may be a disadvantage, so even רבי יהודה agrees they must be told.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the case is a courtyard located between two alleyways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the 'no dispute' view. It says the משנה from Step 23 is a special case where everyone agrees notice is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard between two alleyways can join either one. Putting it into one alleyway's עירוב might stop it from joining the other, which it may have preferred. Since this is not clearly a benefit, they must be informed, and רבי יהודה would agree.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that other משנה)
A courtyard between two alleyways

phrases.english: There, it is a courtyard between two alleyways.
phrases.notes: Joining one alleyway may cost them the other, so it is not a pure benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּחָצֵר שֶׁבֵּין שְׁנֵי מְבוֹאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 23 by narrowing the case of that משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires informing in every case, against רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה deals only with a courtyard between two alleyways, where joining may be a disadvantage. Even רבי יהודה agrees they must be informed there.

steps.title: רב חסדא says his colleagues do disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. רב שיזבי quoted רב חסדא as learning from that very משנה that רבי יהודה's colleagues disagree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב שיזבי say in the name of רב חסדא: this proves that רבי יהודה's colleagues disagree with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the answer of Step 24. It brings an אמורא who read the same משנה as a real dispute with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 tried to fit the משנה with רבי יהודה by limiting it to a special courtyard. But רב חסדא understood that משנה as showing other תנאים argue with רבי יהודה about informing. That supports the idea of a dispute, which fits שמואל's wording 'הלכה'.

keyTerms.meaning: This proves / this teaches
His colleagues disagree with him

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the discussion back toward a real dispute between רבי יהודה and the חכמים. That helps explain why שמואל would rule 'הלכה כרבי יהודה'.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Sheizvi say in the name of Rav Chisda:
This proves

phrases.aramaic: חֲלוּקִין עָלָיו חֲבֵירָיו עַל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: that his colleagues disagree with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 24 by citing an אמורא who read the same משנה as a dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה deals only with a courtyard between two alleyways, where even רבי יהודה agrees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא learned from this משנה that רבי יהודה's colleagues disagree with him. So the משנה cannot be a case where everyone agrees.

steps.title: Dropping the failed answer and preparing a new one
steps.stepSummary: With the single word אלא, the גמרא gives up the courtyard-between-two-alleyways answer and signals that a new resolution is coming.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It says "Rather" to show that the last answer no longer works and a new answer is about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25, רב חסדא's reading of the משנה showed that רבי יהודה's colleagues do disagree with him. That broke the answer from step 24. The word אלא admits the old answer is gone and opens a fresh approach meant to settle both difficulties together: רב אחא's question (step 22) and רב חסדא's statement (step 25).

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather". It drops the previous answer and introduces a new one.

steps.confusionAlert: אלא here does not mean "except" or "only". When it opens a sentence after an answer has been knocked down, it means "Rather": the old answer is thrown out and a new one is coming.
